root_cause.text: `f2fs_compress_write_end_io()` in the F2FS compressed writeback path decremented `F2FS_WB_CP_DATA` too early, allowing concurrent unmount to free `sbi` and destroy `sbi->page_array_slab` before the callback finished using `sbi` in `page_array_free()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `dec_page_count(sbi, type)` from before `atomic_dec_return(&cic->pending_pages)`/`page_array_free()` to after `page_array_free()` and adds a comment that it must be “the last access to sbi” because dropping the counter to zero lets unmount destroy `sbi` and `sbi->page_array_slab`; the CVE description explicitly says the old ordering let `f2fs_put_super()` proceed to `f2fs_destroy_page_array_cache(sbi)` and `kfree(sbi)` while `page_array_free(sbi, ...)` was still executing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compressed write completion accounting by moving the page count decrement into the early-return path based on pending page tracking.
intent_record.what: In f2fs_compress_write_end_io(), the decrement of the per-type page count was moved from before the pending_pages atomic decrement to inside the conditional branch that returns early when pending_pages is still nonzero. The code now decrements page_count only when atomic_dec_return(&cic->pending_pages) evaluates true; otherwise it falls through to the loop handling the remaining pages.
intent_record.how: This changes the accounting order so the page count is only decremented on the early-return path, while the final completion path no longer performs that decrement before processing the remaining referenced pages. It affects runtime state tracking for compressed write completion and likely corrects mismatched page accounting tied to pending compressed pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move dec_page_count() to the end of f2fs_compress_write_end_io() to avoid use-after-free during unmount teardown.
intent_record.what: In f2fs_compress_write_end_io(), after freeing the page array and the cic object, the code now calls dec_page_count(sbi, type) at the end, with a new comment explaining that this must be the last access to sbi.
intent_record.how: This changes the ordering so that the writeback page count is decremented only after all other uses of sbi are finished, reducing the chance that unmount can free sbi or sbi->page_array_slab while this completion path is still accessing them.

Move dec_page_count() to the end of f2fs_compress_write_end_io() to avoid use-after-free during unmount teardown.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets compressed write completion accounting in f2fs_compress_write_end_io(), which matches the root cause of decrementing F2FS_WB_CP_DATA too early and racing with unmount/sbi teardown.

The change directly matches the reported root cause: `f2fs_compress_write_end_io()` was decrementing `F2FS_WB_CP_DATA` too early, and moving `dec_page_count()` to the end prevents unmount teardown from freeing `sbi`/`page_array_slab` before the callback finishes.

candidates.rationale: This decrements the writeback/compressed-data accounting too early. In the vulnerable flow, the callback can continue to use `sbi` after this point, so unmount teardown may free `sbi` and its slab before `page_array_free()` finishes, causing a use-after-free.
This is the later use of `sbi` that becomes unsafe once `dec_page_count()` has already allowed teardown to proceed. The root cause manifests when this function runs after `sbi` may have been freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement decrements the writeback/compressed-data accounting too early in f2fs_compress_write_end_io(), which can let concurrent unmount teardown proceed and free sbi and sbi->page_array_slab before the callback finishes using sbi.
This later use of sbi becomes unsafe once dec_page_count() has already been executed, because teardown may free sbi before page_array_free() completes.
